To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

PKA-mediated phosphorylation of cardiac myosin binding proteins accelerates the cross-bridge cycling rate and contributes to the enhanced systolic performance observed during &bgr; adrenergic stimulation.
PKA phosphorylated cMyBP-C is required for the PKA-mediated acceleration of the stretch activation response and the rate of force production in skinned murine myocardium.
ablation of the myofilament protein cMyBP-C eliminates the effect of PKA treatment to accelerate the stretch activation response of murine skinned myocardium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the &bgr;-agonist response in cardiac muscle.
the role of cMyBP in cardiac contractility.
understanding the molecular basis for the regulation of the mechanical properties of muscle by the cardiac myofilaments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the phosphorylation of cTnI by PKA is the major mechanism for the acceleration of the twitch kinetics in cardiac muscle, but that the phosphorylation and/or the binding of cMyBP to cTnI may also be involved.
PKA-mediated acceleration of cross-bridge cycling in murine myocardium is mediated through cMyBP-C, but that cMyBP-C may not be the sole target of PKA in this system.
PKA phosphorylates cMyBP-C, and this phosphorylation accelerates the rate at which the cross-bridge cycle can be completed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

PKA-mediated acceleration of the stretch activation response is dependent upon phosphorylation of cTnI, whereas acceleration of force redevelopment is dependent upon phosphorylated cTnI and phosphorylated cMyBP-C.
cMyBP-C is a key regulator of cardiac contractility.
cMyBP-C plays a role in the PKA-mediated enhancement of the rate of force production, and this effect is likely due to the acceleration of the rate of cross-bridge cycling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cMyBP-C is a major target of PKA in the heart and plays a key role in mediating the &bgr;-agonist effects on contractility in vivo.
cMyBP-C is an essential mediator of the effects of PKAcatalyzed phosphorylation on the rate of myofilament force generation.
cMyBP-C phosphorylation contributes to the acceleration of cross-bridge kinetics in response to &bgr;-agonist stimulation.
